ZERO LIMITS

We are a multidisciplinary team with skills in AI, Data Science, Web Development, and Flutter. We’re passionate about exploring Earth systems, solving real-world problems, and turning complex NASA data into clear, engaging, and meaningful digital experiences.
summary:
What did you develop?
Earthanova is a web platform that turns NASA Earth data into a "data detective" experience. Users pick any place on land on an interactive 3D globe, or search for a city, choose a study period and scan it. The platform pulls up to 45 years of NASA data: NASA POWER climate (temperature, rain, solar energy, soil wetness), GPM IMERG rainfall, MERRA-2 air quality and dust, NASA-SSH sea level and NASA EONET events, plus clearly labelled non-NASA sources (USGS earthquakes, Esri historical imagery). It runs trend tests (Mann-Kendall with Sen's slope) and shows the results in three modes: Basic for the public, Advanced for researchers and Playful for students.

How does it address the challenge?
Earth data is vast, scattered and usually needs expertise to interpret. Earthanova retrieves and analyses it automatically, then explains each result in plain words: real, maybe real, or just chance. For Alexandria, for example, it finds significant warming of +0.29 °C per decade from 1981 to 2025. Non-significant results are shown, not hidden. Risk Monitoring and a Compare page for two places are included.

Why is it important?
It closes the gap between having data and understanding it. Students learn how scientists decide whether a trend is real, and communities see how their own place is changing. It is free, needs no account and stores no personal data.
details:
What it does

Earthanova turns NASA Earth data into a "data detective" experience for high-school and college students and the scientifically curious public. Pick any place on land on a 3D globe and scan it. The app pulls 45 years of NASA data for that point, finds the trends and tells you, in plain words, whether each change is real, maybe real, or just chance.

How it works

- Climate (1981-2025): NASA POWER monthly temperature, maximum temperature, rainfall, solar energy and root-zone soil wetness (~50 km grid).

- Rainfall from space: NASA GPM IMERG V07.

- Air quality: PM2.5 and desert dust from NASA MERRA-2 aerosol diagnostics.

- Sea level: NASA-SSH satellite altimetry. Natural events: NASA EONET.

- Statistics computed in the browser: Mann-Kendall trend test, Sen's slope with a 95% interval, linear regression p-values, anomalies, correlations.

Three views for three kinds of user:

- Basic: clue cards with a clear verdict and "evidence dots".

- Advanced: variable explorer, warming stripes, heatmaps, scatter plots, correlation matrix, trend table and data export.

- Playful: case-file quizzes, a climate fingerprint for your birth year, and a "beat the forecast" game.

Risk Monitoring shows heat, drought, flood, dust and sea-level trends with a hazard calendar and a map of recent events. Compare sets two places side by side for trip dates, using a NASA trend-adjusted outlook built from 30 years of daily NASA POWER data, with a reliability check. A short-range weather forecast (Open-Meteo) appears only for trip days within 16 days and is clearly labelled "Not NASA".

Benefits and impact

It closes the gap between having data and understanding it. Students learn how scientists decide whether a trend is real; teachers get ready-made, local case studies; communities and travellers can see how their own place is changing.

Tools

Next.js, React, TypeScript, globe.gl / three.js and hand-built SVG charts on the front end; a Python (Starlette) API with SQLite on the back end, pulling NASA data through the NASA POWER API, Earthdata CMR and OPeNDAP. Hosted on Vercel and a Hetzner VPS. Source code: https://github.com/zzzq0681-cz/earthanova

What makes it creative

Statistics become detective work: a verdict, evidence and a "chance" score instead of bare p-values. The same data serves a beginner, a researcher and a student playing a game.

Factors we considered

Honesty about uncertainty: non-significant results are shown, not hidden; modelled data is labelled as modelled; the ~50 km grid is explained; points in open water are refused because land data does not exist there. Every non-NASA source is labelled. No login and no personal data; reports are kept only for the visit. The app works on phones, tablets and desktops.
